qs.q: Which of the following are signs of a rupturing AAA? (A) Increased BP (B) Decreased Hct (C) Low back pain (D) Decreased BP (E) Intermittent abdominal pain
qs.ex: الـ AAA لما يتقطع: وجع شديد في الضهر أو البطن، والضغط بيقع، والـ Hct بيقل (نزيف)، وفيه pulsatile mass.

ev.txt: Classic Triad: 60–70 y/o … abdominal pain, hypotension, and a pulsatile abdominal mass and/or shock … Rate of Enlargement: 0.5 cm / year … 50% die prior to reaching hospital

qs.q: Which of the following surgical technique allows for shorter recovery times after aortic aneurysm ?
qs.ex: الـ EVAR (endovascular graft): إجراء minimally invasive، والتعافي أسرع، والإقامة في المستشفى أقصر.

ev.txt: EVAR … Less pain — Faster recovery & shorter hospital stay … Disadvantages — Need regular follow-up scans … Slight risk of stent graft migration

qs.q: ……….. is BP usually >180/120 WITH impending or progressing end-organ damage
qs.ex: الـ Hypertensive emergency: ضغط أكتر من 180/120 مع end-organ damage. الـ urgency من غير damage.

ev.txt: Hypertensive Urgency: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … ABSENCE of end-organ damage … oral antihypertensives. Hypertensive Emergencies: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … PRESENCE of end-organ damage … IV medications

qs.q: Increased myoglobin level in a patient with chest pain suggests ………
qs.ex: الـ myoglobin العالي مع ألم الصدر = علامة بدرية للـ MI. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following lab, results is a predictor of evidence of myocardial injury ?
qs.ex: الـ CK-MB مخصوص لعضلة القلب، ودليل على الـ injury. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following is a contraindication for Nitroglycerine administration ?
qs.ex: الـ Nitroglycerin ممنوع لو الـ SBP أقل من 90 (hypotension)، علشان بيوسّع الأوعية.

ev.txt: Sodium nitroprusside Vasodilator Immediate … thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity … Nitroglycerin … Hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache

qs.q: The nurse expects a patient to develop which of the following common side effects of Nitroglycerin infusion ?
qs.ex: أشهر عرض جانبي للـ Nitroglycerin: الصداع، لأنه بيوسّع أوعية المخ.

ev.txt: Sodium nitroprusside Vasodilator Immediate … thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity … Nitroglycerin … Hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache

qs.q: Dobutamine hydrochloride (Dobutrex) is indicated for treatment of patients with which of the following diagnosis ?
qs.ex: الـ Dobutamine (positive inotrope) للـ CHF والـ cardiogenic shock. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: When administering thrombolytic drugs, it is important for the nurse to:
opts: Know that drug action will vary according to the dose.
Observe the patient for bleeding during infusion.
Send a blood sample for assessing the kidney function.
qs.ex: الـ thrombolytics أخطر مضاعفاتها النزيف، وأخطره intracranial hemorrhage. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following manifestations indicate that a patient is having a hypertensive emergency ?
opts: An elevated systolic BP >180 with evidence of acute organ disease.
A systolic BP >200 mm Hg with an absence of organ dysfunction.
A sudden rise in BP >160 mm Hg & accompanied by a severe headache.
A severe elevation of BP that occurs over several weeks or months.
qs.ex: الـ Hypertensive emergency: ضغط أكتر من 180/120 مع end-organ damage. الـ urgency من غير damage.

ev.txt: Hypertensive Urgency: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … ABSENCE of end-organ damage … oral antihypertensives. Hypertensive Emergencies: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … PRESENCE of end-organ damage … IV medications

qs.q: While monitoring a patient with an acute decompensated heart failure accompanied by compromised respiratory functions, you would expect which of the following complications?
qs.ex: الـ Decompensated HF مع مشاكل في التنفس = pulmonary edema.

ev.txt: Complications of Hypertensive Emergencies: Retinal hemorrhages … Pulmonary edema … MI … Hemorrhagic stroke … Renal involvement … Cerebral edema → seizures and coma.

qs.q: Which of the following measures should the nurse Include in the plan of care for a patient with ruptured aortic aneurysm ?
opts: Preparation for intra aortic balloon pump insertion.
qs.ex: الـ ruptured aneurysm: antihypertensives و negative inotropes، وأكسجين، ومسكنات، وسوائل ودم.

ev.txt: Emergency Management of Dissecting/Ruptured Aneurysm: Administer antihypertensives. Administer negative inotropic agents … oxygen … narcotics for pain … IV fluids and blood transfusions

qs.q: The highest nursing management priority for a patient with decompensated heart failure during the acute phase is to:
opts: Monitor daily weight and urine output
Teach the patient on medications and diet
Permit unrestricted amount of fluid intake
qs.ex: أولوية الـ acute phase: نزوّد الـ cardiac output والـ organ perfusion. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Reduction of myocardial oxygen consumption in patients with decompensated heart failure is best achieved through
qs.ex: تقليل الـ afterload بيقلل شغل القلب واستهلاكه للأكسجين. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: A patient is diagnosed as having hypertensive emergency when the BP is. .....and his kidney function test...
qs.ex: الـ Hypertensive emergency: ضغط أكتر من 180/120 مع end-organ damage. الـ urgency من غير damage.

ev.txt: Hypertensive Urgency: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … ABSENCE of end-organ damage … oral antihypertensives. Hypertensive Emergencies: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … PRESENCE of end-organ damage … IV medications

qs.q: Furosemide is prescribed in combination with sodium Nitroprusside in order to:
opts: Decrease cardiac worklead by decreasing afterload.
Increase potassium excretion to prevent hyperkalemia.
qs.ex: الـ Furosemide مع الـ nitroprusside علشان يمنع احتباس الملح والمية (الـ vasodilators بتنشّط الـ RAAS). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following findings is alarming manifestation that requires rapid assessment for patient with aortic aneurysm:
qs.ex: Hb 7 = أنيميا شديدة، بتقلل توصيل الأكسجين للقلب. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Sodium Nitroprusside solution must be protected from light with an opaque sleeve to:
opts: Prevent degradation of the medication by light.
qs.ex: الضوء بيكسّر الـ nitroprusside، فبنغطيه بغطا معتم (opaque sleeve). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: In patient with hypertensive crises Bp should be rapidly lowered to 120/80 mmHg
qs.ex: غلط: منقللش الضغط لـ 120/80 بسرعة. بنقلل الـ MAP مش أكتر من 25% في أول ساعة.

ev.txt: Golden Target Goal: Reduce the mean blood pressure (MAP) by NO MORE THAN 25% within 1 hour of starting treatment (to avoid hypoperfusion).

qs.q: Localized dilatation of the aorta 50% over the normal diameter is characterizing for aortic dissection.
qs.ex: غلط: الاتساع 50% فوق القطر الطبيعي ده تعريف الـ true aneurysm. الـ dissection معناها انفصال الـ media بعمود دم.

ev.txt: Aortic Aneurysm (True Aneurysm): Localized dilatation of the aorta 50% over the normal diameter. Includes all three layers … Pseudoaneurysm: Collection of blood and connective tissues outside the aortic wall. Dissecting Aneurysm: Longitudinal separation of the medial layers

qs.q: The resistance of the blood, valves, and blood vessels that the left ventricle must overcome to eject blood is known as preload.
qs.ex: غلط: المقاومة اللي الـ LV بيقاومها علشان يضخ الدم اسمها afterload، مش preload. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following drugs is most commonly administered to treat hypertensive emergency
qs.ex: الـ Sodium nitroprusside أشهر علاج للـ HTN emergency، ومفعوله فوري.

ev.txt: Sodium nitroprusside Vasodilator Immediate … thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity … Nitroglycerin … Hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache

qs.q: In electrocardiogram, the P wave represents ………..
qs.ex: الـ P wave = atrial depolarization. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: The inherent rate of the Purkinje fibers is:
qs.ex: الـ Purkinje من 20 لـ 40. الـ AV/His من 40 لـ 60. الـ SA من 60 لـ 100. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: The property of cardiac muscle cells to shorten fiber's length in response to electrical stimulation is called:
qs.ex: الـ Contractility: الألياف بتقصر لما تتنبّه كهربيًا. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: To gather information about impulse conduction from the atria to the ventricles, you have to study the:
qs.ex: الـ PR interval = التوصيل من الـ atria للـ ventricles. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: If a lead comes off the patient's chest, the waveform:
opts: won't be seen at all on the monitor
qs.ex: لو الـ lead اتشال، مش هيظهر waveform خالص (flat line). لازم نتأكد من المريض قبل ما نحكم إنه asystole. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: QRS represent ventricular depolarization and its duration should be 3 small squares
qs.ex: غلط: الـ QRS بيمثّل ventricular depolarization، بس مدته الطبيعية من 0.06 لـ 0.10 ثانية (أقل من 3 مربعات صغيرين). (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: Which is the best area for auscultating the apical pulse ?
qs.ex: الـ apical pulse في الـ mitral area (المسافة الخامسة، على خط نص الترقوة الشمال). (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: In regular rhythm, ventricular rate can be determined by counting the number of small boxes between two consecutive:
qs.ex: الـ Rate = 1500 ÷ عدد المربعات الصغيرة بين R و R. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: To gather information about impulse conduction from the atria to the ventricles, you have to study the:
qs.ex: الـ PR interval = التوصيل من الـ atria للـ ventricles. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: When a patient is admitted to the ICU, his heart rate is 33 beats/min. which area of the heart is most likely to serve as the pacemaker ?
qs.ex: نبض 33 = إيقاع من الـ Purkinje (من 20 لـ 40). (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: What is the inherent rate of the Bundle of His ?
qs.ex: الـ Bundle of His من 40 لـ 60. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: The cardiac property in which non-pacemaker cells can respond to impulse and depolarize is called:
qs.ex: الـ Excitability: الخلايا بتستجيب للتنبيه وبتعمل depolarization. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: Elevation or depression of the ST segment by 0.2 mV from the baseline is considered normal.
qs.ex: غلط: ارتفاع أو انخفاض الـ ST بـ 0.2 mV مش طبيعي، ده بيدل على ischemia أو injury. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: If the sinus node was diseased, ischemic and no longer firing as the heart's primary pacemaker, which rhythm would you expect as a normal compensatory mechanism?
qs.ex: لو الـ SA وقف، الـ AV junction هو اللي بيمسك (junctional rhythm من 40 لـ 60). (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: P wave in the junctional rhythm will be:
opts: Normal in configuration and before each QRS
Twice as frequently as the QRS
Absent as the impulses start at the SA node
qs.ex: في الـ junctional الـ P wave بتبقى inverted قبل أو بعد الـ QRS، أو مش موجودة. (ECG – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), proper hand placement for chest compressions is essential to reduce the risk of:
qs.ex: لو مكان الإيد غلط في الـ CPR، أشهر مضاعفة كسر في الضلوع. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What causes the pain that occurs with myocardial ischemia?
opts: Lactic acid accumulation during anaerobic metabolism
Elevated pressure in the ventricles and pulmonary vessels
qs.ex: ألم الـ ischemia سببه تراكم lactic acid من الـ anaerobic metabolism. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: When a patient reports chest pain, why must unstable angina be identified and rapidly treated?
opts: The pain may be severe and disabling
ECG changes and dysrhythmias may occur during an attack
Atherosclerotic plaque deterioration may cause complete thrombus of the vessel lumen
Because it occurs due to spasm of a major coronary artery which may increase chest pain
qs.ex: الـ unstable angina معناها إن الـ plaque بتتدهور، وممكن تتحول لـ MI. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Unstable angina is distinguished from Non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) by which of the following criteria?
qs.ex: الـ NSTEMI = ST depression مع troponin عالي. الـ UA = troponin طبيعي. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: A patient has been managed angina episodes with nitroglycerin. Which of the following indicates that the drug is effective?
qs.ex: الـ nitroglycerin شغال = ألم الصدر قلّ.

ev.txt: Sodium nitroprusside Vasodilator Immediate … thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity … Nitroglycerin … Hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache

qs.q: Which of the following is most appropriate for a patient during the acute phase of myocardial infarction?
opts: Increase IV fluids in the first 24 hrs
Provide bed rest with bedside commode
qs.ex: الـ acute MI: راحة في السرير، ويستعمل bedside commode. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following lab. results is a predictor of evidence of myocardial injury?
qs.ex: الـ CK-MB مخصوص لعضلة القلب، ودليل على الـ injury. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: The nurse should monitor a patient with an acute myocardial infarction who is receiving intravenous streptokinase (Streptase) for which of the following serious side effects?
qs.ex: الـ thrombolytics أخطر مضاعفاتها النزيف، وأخطره intracranial hemorrhage. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: To detect and treat the most common complication of MI, what should the nurse do?
opts: Keep the patient NPO for the first 24 hours
Take vital signs every 2 hours for the first 8 hours
qs.ex: أشهر مضاعفة للـ MI: dysrhythmias، وكمان HF. نسمع الصدر علشان crackles (pulmonary edema). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: The primary effective method to determine the location of myocardial infarction is:
qs.ex: الـ 12-lead ECG بيحدد مكان الـ MI. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: The preferred and MOST diagnostic biomarker for a patient with myocardial infarction is:
qs.ex: الـ Troponin هو أكتر biomarker مخصوص وتشخيصي. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following is the main outcome when administering nitroglycerin for a patient with ACS?
qs.ex: الـ nitroglycerin بيوسّع الشرايين التاجية، فيقلل الألم.

ev.txt: Sodium nitroprusside Vasodilator Immediate … thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity … Nitroglycerin … Hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache

qs.q: When administering a thrombolytic drug to a patient with acute MI, the nurse explains that the purpose of this drug is to:
qs.ex: الـ thrombolytics بتدوّب الجلطة. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What would be the MOST effective treatment for ACS within 90 minutes of symptoms onset?
qs.ex: الـ PCI أحسن علاج، و door-to-balloon أقل من 90 دقيقة. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: The diagnostic criteria of acute myocardial infarction includes:
qs.ex: الـ ST elevation من معايير الـ MI (STEMI). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Medical management of a patient with ACS includes which of the following medications? (1) B-blockers (2) Morphine sulphate (3) Heparin (4) Noradrenaline
qs.ex: علاج الـ ACS: beta-blockers، و morphine، و heparin (MONA-BH). الـ Noradrenaline مش منهم. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: According to American Heart Association (AHA) statistics, what is the global epidemiological significance of acute cardiovascular emergencies?
opts: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, with an acute coronary event occurring roughly every 40 seconds.
Cardiovascular disease is the third leading cause of death, superseded by primary endocrine dysfunction.
Cardiovascular mortality has been completely eradicated in patients under 65 years of age.
Acute coronary events occur exclusively in individuals with documented hereditary muscular dystrophy.
qs.ex: أمراض القلب أول سبب للوفيات في العالم. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Why can cardiovascular emergencies easily be missed or misdiagnosed in the emergency department?
opts: Because 12-lead ECG machines automatically filter out abnormal waveforms in emergency mode.
Because they frequently present with subtle, minor, or atypical signs and symptoms that mimic benign conditions unless clinicians maintain a high index of suspicion.
Because cardiac troponin only enters the systemic circulation in patients older than 90 years.
Because myocardial ischemia is physiologically restricted to the abdominal wall muscles.
qs.ex: ممكن تيجي بأعراض atypical، فتتفوّت.

ev.txt: Cardiovascular emergencies can present with typical or atypical signs and symptoms. Some patients have such minor complaints that they can be missed

qs.q: Which patient populations are at the highest risk for presenting with 'silent' or atypical myocardial infarction?
opts: Young athletic male patients with completely normal resting lipid panels.
Pediatric patients undergoing routine tonsillectomy procedures.
Diabetic patients with autonomic neuropathy, elderly individuals, and female patients.
Patients with isolated unilateral benign essential tremor.
qs.ex: مرضى السكر (autonomic neuropathy) والستات والكبار في السن بيجيلهم MI صامت أو atypical. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: During which phase of the cardiac cycle does myocardial perfusion through the coronary arteries predominantly occur?
opts: Exclusively during peak ventricular systole when aortic pressure is at its maximum.
During the isovolumetric contraction phase while the mitral valve snaps shut.
Continuously and equally throughout both systole and diastole without variation.
Exclusively during ventricular DIASTOLE, when aortic root backpressure fills the coronary ostia behind the closed aortic valve.
qs.ex: الدم بيوصل لعضلة القلب في الـ diastole. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Occlusion of the Left Anterior Descending (LAD) coronary artery carries high mortality and is colloquially termed the 'Widow Maker' because:
opts: It is the only blood vessel supplying venous drainage to the coronary sinus.
It supplies the vast majority of the anterior left ventricular wall and the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum.
It selectively perfuses the right atrial appendage and pulmonary trunk.
It carries deoxygenated blood directly from the inferior vena cava.
qs.ex: الـ LAD «widow maker» علشان بيغذّي معظم الـ LV من قدام والـ septum. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the clinical significance of Jugular Venous Distension (JVD) assessed at a 45- degree angle in a cardiac patient?
opts: It provides an accurate non-invasive physical reflection of elevated Right Atrial Pressure and Central Venous Pressure (CVP).
It indicates an immediate rupture of the external carotid artery.
It confirms adequate arterial oxygen saturation in the cerebral cortex.
It is an exclusive sign of acute bacterial meningitis.
qs.ex: الـ JVD على 45° تقييم غير تدخلي للـ CVP والـ right heart. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the international emergency standard for the time window to obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG in a patient presenting with acute chest discomfort?
opts: Within 45 to 60 minutes after initial laboratory blood draws are completed.
Within 120 minutes following inpatient admission to the cardiac telemetry floor.
Only after serial troponin results confirm myocardial necrosis.
Within 10 minutes of arrival at the emergency department door.
qs.ex: الـ ECG خلال 10 دقايق من الوصول. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Auscultation of an abnormal S3 heart sound ('ventricular gallop') in an adult presenting with acute dyspnea indicates:
opts: Closure of the aortic and pulmonic valves during ventricular systole.
Atrial contraction against a stiff, hypertrophic ventricular wall in chronic hypertension.
Sudden deceleration of blood entering a volume-overloaded, dilated left ventricle during early diastole, characteristic of acute heart failure.
Benign turbulence within the inferior vena cava secondary to heavy exercise.
qs.ex: الـ S3: الدم بيقف فجأة وهو داخل ventricle متوسع، وده علامة HF. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following is classified as a NON-MODIFIABLE risk factor for cardiovascular disease?
opts: Advancing age, biological male gender, and family history of premature coronary artery disease.
Cigarette smoking and chronic nicotine vaping.
Sedentary lifestyle and lack of aerobic exercise.
Atherogenic dyslipidemia and elevated dietary trans-fat intake.
qs.ex: العوامل اللي ماتتغيرش: السن، والجنس (ذكر)، والوراثة.

ev.txt: RISK FACTORS — A. Inherited & Adaptable: Genetic predisposition, Hypertension, Older age, Diabetes, lipids · B. Behavioral or Modifiable: Smoking | Sedentary lifestyle | Obesity | High-fat diet

qs.q: What is the pathognomonic physical finding known as 'Levine's Sign' in a patient experiencing acute myocardial ischemia?
opts: The patient experiences sharp right upper quadrant pain upon deep inspiration during liver palpation.
The patient displays bilateral pupillary constriction when exposed to ambient light.
The patient instinctively clenches a fist over the sternum to describe the severe, squeezing retrosternal pressure.
The patient holds both arms behind the back to relieve thoracic pain.
qs.ex: الـ Levine's sign: المريض بيقفل إيده على صدره. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What are the recommended chest compression rate and depth benchmarks for high-quality adult CPR according to AHA guidelines?
opts: Rate of 60 to 80 compressions per minute, and depth of 1 inch (2.5 cm).
Rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute, and depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm) up to 2.4 inches (6 cm).
Rate of 140 to 160 compressions per minute, and depth of 3.5 inches (9 cm).
Rate of 80 to 100 compressions per minute, with depth variable based on rescuer preference.
qs.ex: من 100 لـ 120 ضغطة في الدقيقة، وعمق من 5 لـ 6 سم. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Why is allowing COMPLETE chest wall recoil between compressions critical during cardiopulmonary resuscitation?
opts: It prevents gastric contents from entering the small intestine.
It resets the defibrillator capacitor for the subsequent electrical shock.
It eliminates the need for any supplemental ventilations.
It generates negative intrathoracic pressure that draws venous blood back into the heart, allowing ventricular filling and coronary perfusion.
qs.ex: الـ recoil بيعمل ضغط سالب جوه الصدر، فالدم بيرجع للقلب. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which of the following cardiac arrest rhythms is considered SHOCKABLE during Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS)?
opts: Sinus Bradycardia with prolonged PR interval.
Pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia (pVT) and Ventricular Fibrillation (VF).
Complete Atrioventricular block with narrow QRS escape.
qs.ex: الـ Shockable: pulseless VT و VF. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the mandatory clinical action IMMEDIATELY following the delivery of a defibrillation shock in cardiac arrest?
opts: Immediately resume high-quality chest compressions for 2 minutes without pausing to check the pulse or analyze the rhythm.
Pause for 30 seconds to carefully palpate the carotid pulse.
Immediately administer 2 mg of IV Atropine bolus.
Disconnect the ECG monitor and evaluate bilateral pupillary reflexes.
qs.ex: بعد الـ shock نكمّل CPR فورًا لمدة دقيقتين. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the correct dosing and administration schedule for Epinephrine during adult cardiac arrest?
opts: 0.1 mg IV bolus administered once at the start of resuscitation only.
1 mg IV/IO administered every 3 to 5 minutes.
10 mg IV push administered every 60 seconds until spontaneous circulation returns.
1 mg continuous IV infusion administered over 24 hours via micro-infusion pump.
qs.ex: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO كل 3–5 دقايق. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the first-line antiarrhythmic medication and initial bolus dose for refractory VF/pVT after the third defibrillation shock?
opts: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push with saline flush.
Diltiazem 20 mg slow IV push over 10 minutes.
Digoxin 0.5 mg IV push diluted in 5% dextrose.
Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO push bolus (followed by a second dose of 150 mg if needed).
qs.ex: Amiodarone 300 mg، وبعدها 150 mg. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: A patient in cardiac arrest displays an organized, narrow-complex electrical rhythm at 75 bpm on the monitor, but has NO palpable carotid pulse. The team should:
opts: Identify this as Pulseless Electrical Activity (PEA), withhold electrical shock, continue high- quality CPR, give Epinephrine 1 mg, and search for 5 H's and 5 T's.
Deliver an immediate 200 J unsynchronized defibrillation shock.
Immediately stop CPR and transfer the patient to the MRI suite.
Administer 300 mg of IV Amiodarone bolus immediately.
qs.ex: إيقاع منظّم من غير نبض = PEA (non-shockable). نعمل CPR ونديله epinephrine. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which reversible cause of cardiac arrest is treated with immediate needle thoracostomy decompression?
qs.ex: الـ Tension PTX (من الـ H's و T's) علاجه needle decompression. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What specific pharmacologic antidote is indicated for cardiac arrest secondary to Torsades de Pointes or suspected hypomagnesemia?
opts: Calcium Gluconate 10 grams rapid IV push.
Magnesium Sulfate 1 to 2 grams IV/IO diluted and pushed over 1 to 2 minutes.
qs.ex: الـ Torsades علاجها magnesium sulfate من 1 لـ 2 جم. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the clinical significance of a sudden, abrupt spike in End-Tidal CO2 (EtCO2) to 35-40 mmHg during continuous capnography in CPR?
opts: It indicates that the endotracheal tube has become dislodged into the esophagus.
It is the earliest objective indicator of Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC).
It signals the immediate onset of irreversible cerebral brain death.
It reflects sudden catastrophic rupture of the alveolar capillaries.
qs.ex: الـ EtCO₂ لما يعلى فجأة لـ 35–40 = رجوع الدورة الدموية (ROSC). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the recommended target temperature range for Targeted Temperature Management (TTM) in comatose adults post-cardiac arrest?
opts: Maintained constantly between 32°C and 36°C for at least 24 hours.
Maintained at 25°C using total body immersion in ice water.
qs.ex: الـ TTM من 32 لـ 36 درجة. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: How is Unstable Angina (UA) fundamentally distinguished from Non- ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI)?
opts: Unstable angina always displays persistent ST-segment elevations >=3 mm.
NSTEMI chest pain only occurs following strenuous physical exertion.
Unstable angina is fatal within 5 minutes without surgical intervention.
Cardiac biomarkers (Troponin I and T) remain negative in Unstable Angina, whereas they are elevated in NSTEMI indicating myocardial necrosis.
qs.ex: الـ NSTEMI = ST depression مع troponin عالي. الـ UA = troponin طبيعي. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF indicates an acute myocardial infarction localized to which anatomical myocardial wall, and involving which culprit vessel?
opts: Inferior myocardial wall, typically caused by acute occlusion of the Right Coronary Artery (RCA).
Anterior myocardial wall, caused by acute occlusion of the Left Anterior Descending (LAD).
Lateral myocardial wall, caused by acute occlusion of the Left Circumflex (LCx).
Septal myocardial wall, caused by acute occlusion of the Left Main Coronary Artery.
qs.ex: الـ ST elevation في II و III و aVF = inferior MI (غالبًا الـ RCA). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the international benchmark for 'Door-to-Balloon' time for primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) in acute STEMI?
opts: Less than 30 minutes from emergency department admission.
Less than 90 minutes from patient arrival at a PCI-capable facility.
Less than 180 minutes following coronary angiography.
Within 12 to 24 hours after symptom onset.
qs.ex: الـ Door-to-balloon أقل من 90 دقيقة. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: When is supplemental oxygen administration clinically indicated in an acute coronary syndrome patient under modern AHA guidelines?
opts: Routinely to all chest pain patients at 15 L/min via non-rebreather mask regardless of SpO2.
Only when arterial PaCO2 drops below 20 mmHg.
Never, because oxygen therapy is strictly toxic to cardiac myocytes in all settings.
Only when oxygen saturation (SpO2) is below 94%, or the patient displays respiratory distress, cyanosis, or heart failure.
qs.ex: الأكسجين بس لو الـ SpO₂ أقل من 90%. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the recommended dose and route for Aspirin during the immediate initial management of suspected acute myocardial infarction?
opts: 162 to 325 mg non-enteric coated tablet CHEWED immediately.
81 mg enteric-coated tablet swallowed whole with 500 mL water.
1000 mg IV infusion administered over 2 hours.
325 mg rectal suppository administered after cardiac catheterization.
qs.ex: Aspirin من 162 لـ 325 mg، non-enteric، ويتمضغ. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Sublingual Nitroglycerin administration is ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED in which of the following clinical scenarios?
opts: Hypertensive crisis with pulmonary congestion and SpO2 96%.
Anterior STEMI with heart rate 85 bpm and blood pressure 150/90 mmHg.
Systolic Blood Pressure <90 mmHg, Right Ventricular Infarction, and recent use of Sildenafil (within 24 hours) or Tadalafil (within 48 hours).
Persistent retrosternal chest pain in a patient with a history of penicillin allergy.
qs.ex: الـ Nitroglycerin ممنوع لو الـ SBP أقل من 90 (hypotension)، علشان بيوسّع الأوعية.

ev.txt: Sodium nitroprusside Vasodilator Immediate … thiocyanate and cyanide toxicity … Nitroglycerin … Hypotension, reflex tachycardia, headache

qs.q: Why is a patient with an acute Right Ventricular (RV) Infarction critically dependent on adequate preload?
opts: Because the right ventricle relies on anaerobic glycolysis requiring hypervolemia.
Because the stunned, stiff right ventricle cannot pump forward without elevated filling pressures; venodilators (nitrates/morphine) cause acute hemodynamic collapse.
Because pulmonary capillary wedge pressure must exceed 40 mmHg to prevent valve regurgitation.
Because RV infarction causes immediate renal artery stenosis requiring high pressure.
qs.ex: الـ RV infarction: البطين اليمين متيبّس، ومحتاج preload كفاية، فممنوع nitrates و diuretics. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the emergency positioning priority for a patient presenting with acute decompensated heart failure and flash pulmonary edema?
opts: Strict High Fowler's position with legs dangling over the side of the bed.
Flat supine position with the feet elevated 30 degrees (Trendelenburg).
Prone position to promote dorsal lung recruitment.
qs.ex: الـ Acute HF/pulmonary edema: High Fowler's والرجلين متدلّيين. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the hallmark symptom and classic physical expectoration seen in fulminant acute pulmonary edema?
opts: Thick, tenacious foul-smelling green purulent sputum with high fever.
Dry non-productive cough with unilateral localized expiratory wheeze.
Painful hemoptysis with dark brown 'currant-jelly' gelatinous mucus.
Severe orthopnea, air hunger, bilateral diffuse crackles, and expectoration of pink, frothy sputum.
qs.ex: الـ Pulmonary edema: orthopnea شديدة، وجوع للهوا، وبلغم رغوي وردي (pink frothy sputum). (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: How does Non-Invasive Positive Pressure Ventilation (CPAP / BiPAP) provide rapid therapeutic relief in cardiogenic pulmonary edema?
opts: It selectively constricts the pulmonary capillary bed to eliminate blood flow.
It generates positive airway pressure that physically pushes transudate fluid out of the alveoli, improves gas exchange, and reduces left ventricular afterload.
It neutralizes systemic lactic acidosis by delivering concentrated helium gas.
It replaces the need for any subsequent diuretic or vasodilator therapy.
qs.ex: الـ CPAP/BiPAP بيعمل ضغط موجب، بيطلّع السوائل من الـ alveoli، وبيقلل الـ preload. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is the physiological hallmark of a patient with a modern continuous-flow Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD)?
opts: The patient maintains a bounding, hyperdynamic radial pulse of 180 bpm at all times.
The patient requires mechanical chest compressions continuously during sleep.
The patient typically has NO PALPABLE PERIPHERAL PULSE and standard automated oscillometric blood pressure cuffs fail to register a reading.
The patient has completely absent heart sounds and absent breath sounds bilaterally.
qs.ex: الـ continuous-flow LVAD: غالبًا مفيش نبض محسوس. (LVAD – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: How must blood pressure be measured accurately in a patient with a continuous- flow LVAD?
opts: Using an automated oscillometric digital blood pressure cuff set to pediatric mode.
By measuring venous pressure via a peripheral 22G intravenous cannula.
Blood pressure cannot and should never be measured in any LVAD recipient.
Using a manual sphygmomanometer cuff and a vascular Doppler probe placed over the radial or brachial artery to determine the Doppler MAP.
qs.ex: الضغط بيتقاس بجهاز manual مع Doppler (الـ MAP). (LVAD – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: What is the recommended target Doppler Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) range in an LVAD patient?
qs.ex: الـ MAP المستهدف من 70 لـ 90. (LVAD – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: What is the fundamental safety rule regarding external electrical defibrillation in a patient with an implanted LVAD?
opts: Defibrillation is strictly contraindicated because electrical current permanently detonates the lithium controller batteries.
Defibrillation must be delivered at 1000 Joules monophasic through the patient's lumbar spine.
Defibrillation is safe and indicated for VF/pVT, but electrode pads must NEVER be placed directly over the implanted titanium pump housing in the left subcostal area.
The LVAD must be surgically removed by an on-call surgeon before any defibrillation attempt.
qs.ex: الـ defibrillation آمن ومطلوب مع الـ LVAD. (LVAD – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: Why are standard external chest compressions (CPR) controversial and approached cautiously in an unresponsive LVAD patient?
opts: Compressions permanently reverse the electrical polarity of the home wall power outlet.
Compressions carry a high risk of dislodging the inflow cannula from the LV apex or tearing the aortic anastomosis, resulting in catastrophic fatal hemorrhage.
Compressions induce immediate bilateral pulmonary atelectasis within 10 seconds.
Compressions have no effect because the ribs are replaced by titanium mesh during LVAD surgery.
qs.ex: الـ compressions ممكن تزحزح الـ cannula أو الجهاز. (LVAD – من المرجع العام)

qs.q: What are the three components of the classic, pathognomonic Beck's Triad seen in Cardiac Tamponade?
opts: Severe hypertension, bradycardia, and irregular respiratory pattern (Cushing's Triad).
Abdominal pain, palpable pulsatile mass, and fever with chills.
Chest pain, pericardial friction rub, and widespread ST depression.
Hypotension (with narrow pulse pressure), Jugular Venous Distension (elevated CVP), and Muffled (distant) Heart Sounds.
qs.ex: الـ Beck's triad: hypotension، و JVD، وأصوات القلب مكتومة. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What is 'Pulsus Paradoxus', a key clinical hallmark of acute cardiac tamponade?
opts: An exaggerated drop in Systolic Blood Pressure of greater than 10 mmHg during normal inspiration.
An elevation of systolic blood pressure by 20 mmHg during coughing.
An alternating strong and weak peripheral pulse with a regular heart rate.
A complete absence of blood pressure during voluntary breath holding.
qs.ex: الـ Pulsus paradoxus: الـ SBP بيقع أكتر من 10 mmHg مع الشهيق. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What pathognomonic electrocardiographic finding is produced by the physical swinging of the heart within a massive pericardial effusion?
opts: Continuous delta waves characteristic of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.
Electrical Alternans (alternating beat-to-beat amplitude and axis of the QRS complexes).
Prominent U waves following the T wave in precordial leads.
Widespread reciprocal ST-segment elevation in all 12 leads.
qs.ex: الـ Electrical alternans: سعة الـ QRS بتتغير من نبضة للتانية علشان القلب بيتمرجح في السائل. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: How is Cardiac Tamponade fundamentally distinguished from Tension Pneumothorax during emergency bedside assessment?
opts: In cardiac tamponade, the systolic blood pressure is always extremely elevated above 220 mmHg.
Tension pneumothorax produces muffled heart sounds and electrical alternans.
In cardiac tamponade, breath sounds are bilaterally EQUAL and CLEAR, and the trachea is MIDLINE; in tension pneumothorax, breath sounds are absent unilaterally with tracheal deviation.
Cardiac tamponade causes immediate massive purulent productive sputum.
qs.ex: في الـ tamponade: أصوات التنفس متساوية والقصبة في النص. في الـ tension PTX: القصبة مايلة ومفيش أصوات تنفس في ناحية.

ev.txt: Tension PTX — Deviated trachea … Decreased breath sounds · Cardiac Tamponade — Beck's Triad

qs.q: What is the correct anatomical approach and needle angulation for emergency subxiphoid pericardiocentesis?
opts: Inserted between the xiphoid process and left costal margin at a 45-degree angle to the skin, directed superiorly and posteriorly toward the left shoulder.
Inserted perpendicular (90 degrees) directly through the center of the sternal manubrium.
Inserted horizontally through the right 8th intercostal space midaxillary line aiming toward the spine.
Inserted inferiorly through the umbilicus aimed toward the pubic symphysis.
qs.ex: الإبرة بين الـ xiphoid والضلع الشمال، وناحية الكتف الشمال بزاوية 45°.

ev.txt: Insert needle at xiphoid angle toward left shoulder … Advance at 45° angle

qs.q: During emergency pericardiocentesis under continuous ECG limb-lead monitoring, what ECG change signals that the needle has made direct contact with the ventricular myocardium?
opts: Sudden disappearance of the P wave followed by deep Q waves.
A gradual increase in the PR interval progressing to complete AV block.
Acute ST-segment elevation (injury current), requiring immediate slight withdrawal of the needle.
Total electrical silence (asystole) on all monitoring leads.
qs.ex: لو حصل ST elevation وإحنا بنعمل pericardiocentesis، يبقى الإبرة لمست الـ myocardium، فنرجّعها. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Which hemodynamic profile is diagnostic of Cardiogenic Shock in a patient following an extensive acute anterior myocardial infarction?
opts: Systolic BP >180 mmHg, elevated Cardiac Index (>4.5 L/min/m²), and PCWP <8 mmHg.
Normal blood pressure, normal cardiac output, and absent central venous pressure.
Profound hypotension with elevated systemic vascular resistance and PCWP <5 mmHg.
Persistent Systolic BP <90 mmHg, reduced Cardiac Index (<2.2 L/min/m²), and elevated Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure (PCWP >18 mmHg).
qs.ex: الـ Cardiogenic shock: الـ SBP أقل من 90، و CI قليل، و PAWP عالي. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Why is aggressive, high-volume IV crystalloid fluid resuscitation contraindicated in primary Cardiogenic Shock?
opts: Because crystalloid fluids cause immediate severe systemic alkalosis.
Because the failing left ventricle cannot pump forward; volume loading rapidly increases hydrostatic pressure and precipitates lethal pulmonary edema.
Because IV fluids immediately dissolve all therapeutic coronary stents.
Because crystalloids stimulate immediate hypercalcemic crisis.
qs.ex: الـ LV الفاشل مش قادر يستحمل سوائل زيادة، فيحصل pulmonary edema. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: What hemodynamic criteria define a Hypertensive Crisis according to standard critical care guidelines?
opts: Acute, severe elevation of blood pressure with Systolic BP >180 mmHg and/or Diastolic BP >120 mmHg.
Systolic BP between 130 and 139 mmHg with Diastolic BP between 80 and 89 mmHg.
Diastolic BP >90 mmHg measured on three separate outpatient clinical visits.
A sudden drop in mean arterial pressure below 50 mmHg during exercise.
qs.ex: الـ Hypertensive emergency: ضغط أكتر من 180/120 مع end-organ damage. الـ urgency من غير damage.

ev.txt: Hypertensive Urgency: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … ABSENCE of end-organ damage … oral antihypertensives. Hypertensive Emergencies: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … PRESENCE of end-organ damage … IV medications

qs.q: What is the defining clinical difference between a 'Hypertensive Urgency' and a 'Hypertensive Emergency'?
opts: Hypertensive Emergency only occurs in pregnant patients with pre-existing diabetes.
Hypertensive Urgency requires immediate endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.
Hypertensive Emergency is defined solely by a diastolic pressure exceeding 160 mmHg.
Hypertensive Emergency features acute, life-threatening target organ damage; Hypertensive Urgency features severe BP elevation WITHOUT acute target organ damage.
qs.ex: الـ Hypertensive emergency: ضغط أكتر من 180/120 مع end-organ damage. الـ urgency من غير damage.

ev.txt: Hypertensive Urgency: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … ABSENCE of end-organ damage … oral antihypertensives. Hypertensive Emergencies: SBP > 180 – DBP > 120 … PRESENCE of end-organ damage … IV medications

qs.q: Which of the following clinical findings demonstrates acute target organ damage diagnostic of a Hypertensive Emergency?
opts: Mild chronic bilateral ankle stiffness after waking in the morning.
Hypertensive encephalopathy with papilledema, acute pulmonary edema, acute aortic dissection, or acute renal failure.
Isolated trace proteinuria on a routine outpatient dipstick without symptoms.
Asymptomatic blood pressure of 190/110 mmHg in an ambulatory clinic.
qs.ex: الـ Hypertensive encephalopathy = end-organ damage.

ev.txt: Complications of Hypertensive Emergencies: Retinal hemorrhages … Pulmonary edema … MI … Hemorrhagic stroke … Renal involvement … Cerebral edema → seizures and coma.

qs.q: According to the 'Sacred 25% Rule' in managing Hypertensive Emergencies, what is the maximum recommended reduction in Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) during the first hour?
opts: Reduce MAP immediately by 60% to 70% within the first 10 minutes.
Reduce blood pressure directly to 100/60 mmHg within the first 15 minutes.
Reduce MAP by NO MORE than 20% to 25% within the first hour of parenteral therapy.
Maintain the blood pressure elevated without any reduction for 72 hours.
qs.ex: الـ MAP يقل مش أكتر من 20–25% في أول ساعة.

ev.txt: Golden Target Goal: Reduce the mean blood pressure (MAP) by NO MORE THAN 25% within 1 hour of starting treatment (to avoid hypoperfusion).

qs.q: Why is an abrupt, precipitous drop of blood pressure back to normal levels strictly avoided in chronic hypertensive emergencies?
opts: Because sudden blood pressure reduction causes immediate systemic hyperthermia.
Because chronic hypertension shifts cerebral and renal autoregulatory curves to the right; a precipitous drop causes watershed cerebral infarction and acute tubular necrosis.
Because normal blood pressure causes coronary artery spasm and coronary calcification.
Because the peripheral veins collapse permanently if pressure drops below 150 mmHg.
qs.ex: في الـ HTN المزمن الـ autoregulation بيتظبط على ضغط عالي، فلو نزّلنا الضغط فجأة يحصل ischemia.

ev.txt: Golden Target Goal: Reduce the mean blood pressure (MAP) by NO MORE THAN 25% within 1 hour of starting treatment (to avoid hypoperfusion).

qs.q: What is the critical clinical EXCEPTION to the 25% MAP reduction rule, requiring rapid lowering of Systolic Blood Pressure to 100-120 mmHg within 20 minutes?
opts: Acute Ischemic Stroke with planned permissive hypertension.
qs.ex: الاستثناء: aortic dissection. بنوصّل الـ SBP لـ 100–120 بسرعة. (من المرجع العام – AHA/ACLS، مش مكتوب نصًا في الملخص)

qs.q: Under what clinical conditions is Cyanide Toxicity most likely to occur in a patient receiving Sodium Nitroprusside infusion for a hypertensive crisis?
opts: When the drug is administered as an oral tablet with breakfast.
When the infusion is protected from ambient light by an opaque sleeve.
When the infusion is continued for greater than 72 hours, administered at high rates (>2 mcg/kg/min), or in patients with hepatic or renal impairment.
Only when the patient has a documented allergy to sulfonamides.
qs.ex: الـ Cyanide toxicity بتحصل لو الـ nitroprusside اتاخد أكتر من 72 ساعة.

ev.txt: Cyanide toxicity occurs when Sodium Nitroprusside is used for MORE THAN 72 HOURS … Odor of almonds … Tachycardia … Mental status changes … Metabolic acidosis … Stop medication! … 100% oxygen … Sodium thiosulfate OR Hydroxocobalamin

qs.q: What pathognomonic physical finding and laboratory abnormality characterize Sodium Nitroprusside Cyanide Toxicity?
opts: Fruity acetone breath with profound respiratory alkalosis and hypoglycemia.
Garlic breath odor with elevated serum potassium and thrombocytopenia.
Sweet musty hepatic odor with severe hypocalcemia and hypernatremia.
Distinct odor of bitter almonds on the breath, altered mental status (confusion/agitation), and severe refractory metabolic (lactic) acidosis.
qs.ex: ريحة لوز مر (bitter almond) و metabolic acidosis.

ev.txt: Cyanide toxicity occurs when Sodium Nitroprusside is used for MORE THAN 72 HOURS … Odor of almonds … Tachycardia … Mental status changes … Metabolic acidosis … Stop medication! … 100% oxygen … Sodium thiosulfate OR Hydroxocobalamin

qs.q: What is the specific medical management and antidote protocol for confirmed Sodium Nitroprusside Cyanide Toxicity?
opts: Increase the nitroprusside infusion rate and administer high-dose IV potassium.
Administer 50 grams of activated charcoal via nasogastric tube only.
Immediately discontinue the nitroprusside infusion, administer 100% oxygen, and administer Sodium Thiosulfate and/or Hydroxocobalamin (Vitamin B12a).
Administer IV Naloxone and perform immediate hemodialysis.
qs.ex: نوقف الـ nitroprusside، وأكسجين 100%، و thiosulfate أو hydroxocobalamin.

qs.q: What is the anatomical definition of a True Aortic Aneurysm?
opts: A tear restricted exclusively to the vascular endothelium without diameter enlargement.
A permanent localized dilatation of the aorta exceeding 50% of the normal diameter that involves all three layers of the arterial wall (Intima, Media, and Adventitia).
A temporary muscular spasm of the ascending aorta following cold exposure.
A collection of blood confined strictly within the pericardial sac without aortic involvement.
qs.ex: الـ True aneurysm: اتساع دائم في مكان معين، والـ 3 طبقات.

ev.txt: Aortic Aneurysm (True Aneurysm): Localized dilatation of the aorta 50% over the normal diameter. Includes all three layers … Pseudoaneurysm: Collection of blood and connective tissues outside the aortic wall. Dissecting Aneurysm: Longitudinal separation of the medial layers

qs.q: How does a 'False Aneurysm' (Pseudoaneurysm) differ anatomically from a True Aortic Aneurysm?
opts: In a pseudoaneurysm, there is a breach in the arterial wall, and the pulsating hematoma is contained only by the adventitia or surrounding perivascular connective tissue.
A pseudoaneurysm contains all three intact arterial wall layers dilated symmetrically.
A pseudoaneurysm is formed exclusively by benign cartilaginous metaplasia.
A pseudoaneurysm only occurs in veins and never involves arterial circulation.
qs.ex: الـ Pseudoaneurysm: دم برّه جدار الشريان، ومش الـ 3 طبقات.

qs.q: What is the fundamental underlying pathophysiology of an Aortic Dissection?
opts: Gradual atherosclerotic calcification obliterating the lumen of the femoral artery.
Bacterial endocarditis causing vegetation formation on the tricuspid valve leaflets.
Complete congenital absence of the thoracic and abdominal aorta.
A tear in the tunica intima allows high-pressure systemic blood to enter and separate the layers of the tunica media, creating a false lumen.
